cues.en: It's time to leave our local application or not really leave it, but store the data somewhere else
than just in memory.
Because at the moment, for example, in the course project, whenever you reload the page, all the
data you added, all the meetups you added are lost, they're gone.
And that simply happens because everything is managed in JavaScript at the moment and therefore in memory.
And when you reload the page, this is all dumped and your app restarts and all your memory is gone.
And in addition, even if that were persisted, you could not share it with other users because it's
only on your computer.
It's not somewhere in the internet where other users can get it from.
So of course we also need a server for some of the data we have.
We need to persist our data in a database.
You don't directly communicate to a database from inside svelte that would be highly insecure because
since it's a client side application, all your JavaScript code is exposed and can be viewed by other
users.
And if you put your database credentials in there, that would be bad.
Instead, you send requests to an API, typically to a backend to a rest API or a GraphQL API that exposes
endpoints where you send data to typically in the Json format, and then that backend in turn uses a
database to store your data.
That is how this flow typically works.
And this is therefore exactly what we'll have a look at in this module.
